summary: A note from the Network Information Center on its enterprise phone service, set up in 1971 so ARPANET sites could call the NIC with tolls billed to the NIC. It attaches a list of numbers and explains that a single 800 number would cost far more, about $2200 per month versus about $800. It updates two earlier NIC documents.

eli5.summary: A list of free phone numbers for calling the network's information office, and a note about why one single number would cost too much.

subtitle: Enterprise phone numbers for calling the ARPANET information center.

tldr.problem: ARPANET sites needed a way to call the Network Information Center (NIC) for support, and a centralized toll-free 800 number would be very expensive.
tldr.mechanism: NIC arranged enterprise phone service in 1971, with tolls billed to the NIC. Each region had one or more enterprise or Zenith (regional toll-free) numbers for sites to call.
tldr.outcome: A list of enterprise and Zenith numbers was published and made available online, with the cost kept to about 800 dollars per month versus the 2200 dollars per month for a single 800 number.

today: This administrative note illustrates the operational aspects of running a large research network. While the specific phone service is obsolete, the principle—balancing support accessibility with cost—remains relevant to any network infrastructure operation.

sections.title: Supporting the Network
sections.content: The Network Information Center provided support for ARPANET operations and helped users with technical questions. By 1973, NIC needed to be easily reachable by phone from sites across the network. This RFC updates earlier lists with the current enterprise and Zenith phone arrangements.
sections.eli5: The information center helped people use the network, so they needed a way for people to call them.

sections.title: The Phone Service Arrangement
sections.content:
In September 1971, NIC established enterprise phone service where all ARPANET sites could call the NIC with tolls billed to the NIC itself. Enterprise numbers are special arrangements for specific area code/prefix combinations; even sites in the same area usually need separate arrangements. Zenith numbers are regional toll-free arrangements.

While less convenient than a single 800 number, this arrangement cost approximately 800 dollars per month, compared to about 2200 dollars per month for a unified 800 number.
sections.eli5: Different regions got different phone numbers that all charged to the NIC instead of the caller. It was cheaper than one big toll-free number.

sections.title: Available Numbers
sections.content:
The RFC provides a table of sites and their corresponding enterprise or Zenith numbers, organized by site name. Sites could also access the list online through the NIC's LOCATOR system.

NIC also provided an answering service for calls received outside business hours (5 PM to 8 AM) to report NIC status. Sites without an enterprise number and wishing to obtain one were invited to contact NIC to request service.
sections.eli5: A table showed which number each computer site should call, and there was someone answering outside office hours too.

references.text: NIC 7554. "Enterprise Phone Service to NIC From ARPANET Sites", September 1971.
NIC 7732. "Revised List of Enterprise and Zenith Numbers", October 1971.
